title: Phase 1 Final Sprint — User Portal, Setup Wizard Steps 2-5, Phase 1 Wrap

decisions.title: User portal at /ui uses admin renderer, not a separate layout
decisions.decision: Render /ui with the existing Renderer.PortalHandler, using a dedicated portal_home.tmpl that inherits from the base layout. No separate portal layout engine.
decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES #4 (thin, composable layers) — reuse the existing renderer pattern rather than duplicating layout infrastructure. The admin sidebar is simply hidden on the portal view via CSS; this avoids a second HTML layout with identical nav/footer boilerplate.
alternatives_considered: Separate portal layout with no sidebar
Redirect /ui to /ui/admin/dashboard for admin users only
decisions.chosen_because: Minimal surface: PortalDeps wires Lifecycle+RouteRegistry and the handler builds the view; no new template inheritance machinery required.

decisions.title: App ExternalURL derived from route registry ListAppRoutes, not LookupByName
decisions.decision: Iterate ListAppRoutes() and match by AppID to derive /apps/<name>/ URL.
decisions.rationale: RouteRegistry interface (engine/app/lifecycle.go) does not expose LookupByName. ListAppRoutes() is the only available read path — O(n) per portal render, acceptable for v1 (few apps).
decisions.chosen_because: Zero interface surface change; portal render is not hot-path; v1 app count is small.

decisions.title: Setup wizard steps 2-5 use PRG pattern with query-param state
decisions.decision: Each wizard step is a separate GET page. POST handlers redirect to the next step, passing pool/share names as URL query params (?pool=tank&share=media).
decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES #6 (no hidden state) — wizard state must be visible in the URL so back-button navigation is safe. SQLite-based session state would require a migration and lifetime management.
alternatives_considered: Store wizard state in SQLite session row
decisions.chosen_because: PRG is stateless, works without JS, trivially testable with plain HTTP assertions.

decisions.title: kura init does not start HTTP server or apply storage/share config
decisions.decision: `kura init` only seeds the admin user row in KURA_STATE_DB. Storage and share setup happen via the web wizard or `kura config apply`.
decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #1 (SSOT): config.json is the source of truth for storage and shares. kura init's job is auth bootstrapping only; conflating it with ZFS pool creation would violate SSOT by creating state not tracked in config.json.
alternatives_considered: kura init --config=file.json to apply full config headlessly
decisions.chosen_because: Minimal scope: init seeds auth, daemon applies config. CI pipelines can chain: kura init && kura config apply file.json.

decisions.title: Config export uses ExportAdapter registry, not ApplyAdapter reverse-read
decisions.decision: Added a separate ExportAdapter interface with Snapshot(ctx, *Config). Storage and share engines register via RegisterExporter(). Export() calls all adapters.
decisions.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES #3 (interface seam at every engine boundary) — ApplyAdapter is write-only; reading state back through it would violate single-responsibility. A separate Snapshot interface is the correct seam.
alternatives_considered: Export reads directly from SQLite without engine involvement
decisions.chosen_because: Engine-owned Snapshot keeps the export logic co-located with the engine that understands its own state. The storage engine knows how to reconstruct TopologyEntry from LivePools; the share engine knows its ACL shape.

decisions.title: Language tab shows en as disabled with v1.x badge — no locale switching in v1
decisions.decision: POST /ui/admin/settings/language/save always returns 200 with ja confirmed. en radio is disabled client-side and rejected server-side. No i18n switching code path.
decisions.rationale: VISION.json: v1 ships ja only. DESIGN_PRINCIPLES #8 (ship what works, not what's planned). A fake save that claims to switch locale and then doesn't would be a lie to the user.
decisions.chosen_because: Visible badge 'v1.x' communicates the roadmap intent without implementing it prematurely. The 'saved' banner confirms the round-trip works for future extension.
